Links: [{"title":"strange keybinding alt+shift+plus doesn't show up in macos app menu · ghostty-org/ghostty · Discussion #4007","url":"https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/4007"},{"title":"Ghostty does not respect XKB key remapping rules since W3C rework · ghostty-org/ghostty · Discussion #7356","url":"https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/7356"},{"title":"Problems assigning keybindings for new_split · ghostty-org/ghostty · Discussion #5626","url":"https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/5626"},{"title":"`ctrl+shift+u` can not be overwritten · ghostty-org/ghostty · Discussion #7384","url":"https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/7384"},{"title":"xkb capslock as modifier key not respected for navigation key rebinds · ghostty-org/ghostty · Discussion #8909","url":"https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/8909"},{"title":"[SOLVED]alt + shift to change keyboard layout sometimes doesn't work - Linux Mint Forums","url":"https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?t=461287"},{"title":"custom keybinding question · ghostty-org/ghostty · Discussion #3431","url":"https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/3431"},{"title":"ghostty-shortcuts.md · GitHub","url":"https://gist.github.com/hensg/43bc71c21d1f79385892352a390aa2ca"}]

I found several relevant GitHub discussions about Ghostty keybindings related to Alt+Shift and XKB on Linux. Here are the key findings:

## Main Issues

There is concern about Ghostty working reliably for Linux users without respecting XKB, and some developers believe Ghostty cannot currently function correctly on Linux without honoring XKB mappings.

One specific issue involves keyboard rules like `esc:swapescape`, where the esc key stops working, and this was potentially an unintended side-effect of a W3C input rework.

## Alt+Shift Keybinding Behavior

## Summary

The Ghostty alt+shift keybinding issue on Linux XKB stems from **a W3C input rework in version 1.1.4 that stopped respecting XKB key remapping rules**. Here's the situation:

**The Problem:**
- Ghostty switched to using physical keycodes based on the W3C standard for keyboard input
- This broke XKB remapping rules (like `caps:swapescape`, `alt:swapalt`, etc.) that nearly all other Linux applications honor
- Alt+Shift and other modifier combinations are affected because XKB normally virtualizes these key interpretations

**Why It's Complex:**
- The developers intentionally chose the W3C approach to ensure "keybinds would be based on the correct keys on the actual keyboard"
- This creates a tension between following the W3C standard and respecting Linux's XKB customization layer
- Users expect system-level XKB mappings to work transparently across all applications

**Current Status:**
- PR #8330 was opened to allow special keys to pass through XKB remapping while maintaining W3C compliance for printable characters
- This is a compromise that aims to fix the issue while keeping the W3C standard benefits

If you're experiencing this issue, check if you have a recent version of Ghostty and whether PR #8330 has been merged into your build.
